groups.sentence: Guides, toolkits and curated resources on teaching with AI are available to faculty.
Teaching centers offer AI workshops, consultations and support to faculty.
Instructors may request AI consultation or support from teaching centers, instructional designers or other experts.
The institution provides faculty with training, workshops, resources and support on AI.
Instructors learn what AI tools can and cannot do, including their strengths and limitations.
Instructors try out generative AI tools themselves, including running their own assignments and prompts through them, before setting course policy.
Instructors attend AI workshops, training sessions or courses offered by their institution.
Instructors discuss AI and course approaches with colleagues and seek peer support.
Instructors review the institution's AI guides and teaching resources.
Instructors reflect on how AI affects their courses, their own views and ethical principles before setting policy.
Instructors may use AI-assisted tools, assignment guides and design exercises to build course policies and assignments.
Faculty who teach with AI must be trained.
Support and consultation are available on AI detection, academic integrity and reporting suspected misuse.
Communities of practice, forums and peer events let faculty learn about AI together over time.
Instructors keep learning about AI over time through ongoing development, talks and courses.
Instructors share their AI assignments, syllabus statements and approaches with colleagues.
